div.l: Whiche he seid was / our lady veyl Prologꝰus
He seid that he hadde / a gobet of the seil
That seynt petir / hadde whan that he wente
Vpon the see / tyl IħuIhesu cryst him hente
He hadde a croys / of latoun ful of stonys
And a glas he hadde / pyggys bonys
But wᵗith. thees relykys / whan that he fond
A pore parson dwellyng / vpon lond
Vpon a daye / he get more moneye
Thanne that person / gat in monethis tweye
And thus wyth feyned flaterye and Iapes
He maad the person / and the petyl his apys
But truly to tellen / at last
He was in chirche a noble ecclesiastre
Wel cowde he reedyn / a lesson or astorye
But all ther best / he song an offertorye
For wel he wyst / whanne that song was song
He must preche / and wele a fyle his tong
To wynne sylver / as he wel cowde
Therfor he song / the meryere and lowde
NOw haue I tolde you sothly / in a clause
Thastat / tharray / the noubre / and eek the cause
Why that assembled / was this companye
In southwerk / at this Ientyl hostlerye
That hyht the tabbard / fast bi the belle
But nowe is tyme / to you for to telle
How that we bar vs / that Ilche nyht
Whanne that we were in that hosterye a lyht
And aftir wol I telle / of our vyage
And all the remenaunt / of owr pylgrimage
BVt first I pray you / of your curtesye
That ye ne rette it nohtnoht nowht / my vylanye
Thouh that I plenerly / speke in this maatere
To telle you here mater / and here chere .
